narrative.overview:
Every Luna screen is a kitchen order ticket (KOT) coming out of a thermal printer on a brushed-steel counter. The page background is the counter; a dark printer slot runs across the top; one ticket of thermal paper hangs from it, centred, at most 440px wide and full-width on phones. Everything the person reads or touches is printed on that paper: a masthead, a KOT number with a live timestamp, dashed and solid rules, dotted-leader data lines, printed boxes for input, and one solid ink bar for the primary action. Choices a person has made collapse into printed lines on the same ticket, and the next section prints in with a stepped line-feed reveal.

The ink is near-black, with a second red ink held back for errors, urgency and the DEV stamp, the way a real kitchen printer uses its red ribbon. Printed data is set in Martian Mono, and the wide (112.5%) heavy cut stands in for the thermal printer's double-width bold header. Short plain-language help, the warm human voice from PRODUCT.md, is set in Hanken Grotesk so it reads as a note written beside the print rather than printed data.

Density is one ticket, one job: a single column that grows downward as the flow progresses. Depth comes from physical objects only (the printer's shadow and the paper's drop shadow on the counter). Nothing inside the paper is raised.

Operate surfaces (the Food Heat Map is the first) use a second, approved composition on the same counter: the Pass. The printer becomes a full-width dark printer bar; below it a steel order rail carries ranked tickets; the working area is a printed sheet (the map) beside a torn detail slip; a receipt tape of time runs along the foot. Same paper, same two inks, same type; only the arrangement changes, because an operator is watching many orders, not filling in one.

Donor operate surfaces (home, List food, a donation's status, the donation list) use a third approved arrangement: Snap first. The photo is the listing. A black photo frame with registration corners is the first thing on the screen and doubles as the camera button; the details are printed chips and steppers on a paper sheet beside it (below it on phones); one sticky ink action sits in the thumb zone; and a donation's progress is one ticket torn into coupons, one per stage, that stamp themselves as they complete. The single centred 440px hanging ticket remains the composition for sign-in and sign-up.

The NGO home reuses the donor shell as Today's shift card: the card a kitchen pins to the wall for the day. Waiting food comes first, as white offer tickets torn off the printer with a large countdown and a full-width ink Accept bar; accepted food reprints below as "coming to you" tickets carrying the drop code; the day card (an Open / Full / Closed punch row and an hour strip of the day) sits beside them on desktop and below them on phones.

The delivery partner home is the same shift card turned for a rider: a pickup request prints as an offer ticket, and once accepted the screen becomes the trip slip, one white torn ticket that shows one step at a time (Collect, then Drop) with directions, a call link, a giant 4-digit code field and the step's action bar. Availability is a two-punch Online / Offline row, echoed as a state chip on the printer bar.

The admin agent board uses a fifth arrangement, built to be read off a projector: **Agents at work**. Under the printer bar a torn cast sheet introduces the four agents as die-cut stickers (a pizza slice for the Food Agent, a chef's hat for the Decision Agent, a tiffin for the NGO Agent, a delivery scooter for the Logistics Agent). Below it each listing gets one row on the counter: its order slip with five stage marks and, at the end, a DELIVERED rubber stamp; the hand-offs as ink arrows and paper chits lying on the counter; and four little ticket printers side by side, one per agent, each with its agent's sticker stuck on the housing, an LED and a state word, and a strip of paper printing what that agent did. A second listing prints a second row below. This is the one place colour appears beyond the inks and LEDs, and it lives only on the four stickers (the Colour Stickers rule).
keyCharacteristics: Steel counter, printer slot, one hanging ticket with a zigzag tear edge at the bottom.
Two inks on paper: black for everything, red only for errors, urgency and dev.
Martian Mono for printed data, Hanken Grotesk for helper notes.
Square corners everywhere on paper; boxes are 1.5–2px ink strokes.
Motion is mechanical: stepped print-in, blinking printer LED, tear-off.
Operate surfaces use the Pass: printer bar, order rail of ranked tickets, printed map plus detail slip, receipt time tape.
Donor surfaces use Snap first: photo frame first, printed chips, one sticky ink action, a coupon ticket per donation.
The NGO home is Today's shift card: offer tickets with a countdown and an ink Accept bar first, then the day card.
The partner home is the rider's shift card: a pickup request or the one-step-at-a-time trip slip first, Online / Offline punches on the day card.
The admin agent board is Agents at work: a cast sheet, then per listing an order slip, the hand-off chits on the counter, and four little printers, one per agent.
Two approved exceptions to two inks: a yellow warning slip for a food tag the photo check is unsure about, and the four colour mascot stickers on Agents at work.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Paper carries black ink and red ink, nothing else. Red means something is wrong, urgent or dev-only; if it is not one of those, it is black. Two exceptions are named below: the Unsure Tag rule and the Colour Stickers rule.

rules.name: The LED Stays On The Printer Rule
rules.body: Green and amber belong to the printer's status light. They never appear on the paper as success or warning colours. Warning Yellow is a separate, paler token and is not the LED amber.

rules.name: The Unsure Tag Rule
rules.body: Yellow on paper means exactly one thing: the photo check is not sure a food tag is right, and the donor may keep it. It marks a slip (border, top band, wash), never text, buttons, grades or progress. If the check is sure the tag is wrong, the slip is red; if nothing needs a decision, the slip is black. Do not reach for yellow for any other warning.

rules.name: The Printer And The Note Rule
rules.body: Data, labels and actions are printed in Martian Mono, and sentences a person reads are written in Hanken Grotesk. If it would appear on a real KOT, it is mono.

rules.name: The Double-Width Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is made with weight and the wide cut (800, wdth 112.5), the way a thermal printer does double-width bold, not with colour or size jumps between neighbouring lines.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: Nothing printed on the paper has a shadow. Printed elements show state by inverting (ink fill, paper text) or by changing stroke, never by lifting.

rules.name: The Ink Density Rule
rules.body: Quantity on a map or chart is shown as more or less black ink, never as a hue ramp. Red is reserved for the gap threshold (and for urgency marks tied to it, such as a rail rank or a trend bar under 60%); a value is either a gap or it is black.

rules.name: The Streets Under The Ink Rule
rules.body: When a real street base is shown it is fully desaturated (saturation -1, contrast +0.05, opacity 0.55) and the paper hex grid is hidden, so the tiles read as a faint pencil underlay beneath the ink, never as a second colour source.

rules.name: The Name The Judge Rule
rules.body: When an AI model makes a judgement a person sees, the ticket prints which model made it, and says plainly when no model did.

rules.name: The Read In Motion Rule
rules.body: Anything a person reads on the move (an address, a place name, a note from the kitchen, what to bring) is a places line: a small mono label above, a left-aligned Hanken sentence below. Never set it as a right-aligned, all-caps dotted-leader value.

rules.name: The No Clocking Off Mid-Trip Rule
rules.body: While a trip is live the Offline punch is disabled, not hidden, with a note saying to finish the trip first.

rules.name: The One Step Rule
rules.body: The trip slip shows only the current stop's place, buttons and code; the other step is a faded tab, not a second set of fields.

rules.name: The Colour Stickers Rule
rules.body: Approved by the user for Agents at work: colour lives only on the four mascot stickers, the way stickers are stuck on a kitchen printer; the paper and type stay Luna. A sticker is in full colour only where it is stuck on printer hardware (a station's housing) or introduced on the cast sheet. Anywhere a mascot is printed on paper (inside a printed line) or lies on the counter (the ends of a hand-off arrow) it is the one-ink line version: every fill turns paper, the ink outlines stay ink. Sticker colours never carry meaning: no state, agent label, chit, arrow, LED or text is coloured to match its mascot. There are four mascots and only four.

rules.name: The Newest Line Is Darkest Rule
rules.body: On a printer that keeps printing, only its latest line is set in full ink and 600 weight; earlier lines drop to soft ink, so the room finds what just happened at a glance.

dos: **Do** put sign-in and sign-up flows on one centred ticket (max 440px) hanging from the printer slot on the steel counter.
**Do** build operator surfaces as the Pass: printer bar, order rail of ranked tickets, printed working sheet with a torn detail slip, and a receipt tape for time.

**Do** build donor surfaces Snap first: the donor shell, the photo frame first (edge to edge on phones, the 7-column side on desktop), printed chips and steppers instead of typed fields, and one primary action in the sticky action dock.
**Do** show a donation's progress as one coupon ticket, a coupon per stage, stamping each as it completes; invert the active stage's mark and keep red for a stopped stage only.
**Do** name the AI model on any judgement it makes, and say so plainly when no model judged.
**Do** show quantity on maps and charts as ink density, with red only past the gap threshold and a dashed outline for “nothing here yet”.
**Do** stamp SAMPLE DATA on the printer bar whenever the numbers are not real, and stand in for unbuilt features with a dashed stub box that says what will print there.
**Do** group slip figures under a heading that names the unit and scope, and keep each leader label short.
**Do** record each completed choice as a dotted-leader line on the same ticket, and print the next section in with the stepped reveal.
**Do** use one ink bar per step for the primary action, and let a single-tap choice (like a role row) advance by itself.
**Do** keep red ink for errors, urgency and dev; pair every red message with a plain Hanken sentence that says what to do.
**Do** use Martian Mono for printed data, labels and actions, and Hanken Grotesk for sentences.
**Do** show state on paper by inverting to ink or changing stroke, and use the 2px dashed ink focus ring everywhere.
